payload.criteria:
NINE CRITERIA. Inherits C1-C4 and C6-C8 unchanged. C5 IS REWRITTEN — the owner ruled its definition wrong, not its weight. C9 IS ADDED, because the first pass had no criterion for the thing that should have decided it.

FOUR DECISIONS AT THIS MILESTONE, and the criteria serve all four:
  D-SEARCH — what provides reading and searching. Bears on C1-C6, C9.
  D-GUIDANCE — how applicable rules are selected for a packet. Bears on C7, C8, C5.
  D-REVIEW — how a gate comes to collect its own review. Bears on C5, C9.
  D-ENGINE — how one agent's engine change reaches every agent. Bears on C5, C9, C3.

TWO CRITERIA ARE VETOES rather than weights, stated up front so scoring cannot quietly trade them away.

C1 FRESHNESS — VETO. Definition: a result reflects the bytes as they are NOW, including bytes the agent wrote seconds ago; no staleness window. Lineage: R1, R3, R5; need N2. Why a veto: the agent's dominant pattern is reading back what it just wrote, so a source that tolerates staleness is not a worse option — it is a wrong answer wearing a confident face, which is the failure class this iteration exists to remove.

C2 REACH — VETO. Definition: can address the working tree, git REFS, and material outside the repository, through one surface. Lineage: R5, R6, R7; needs N1, N5. Why a veto: since the close-and-merge split withheld iteration evidence from the working tree, a working-tree-only tool cannot answer 'what did a shipped iteration decide' AT ALL.

C3 ONE-CLICK INSTALLABILITY — weight 5. Definition: a plain install yields a working tool on the target platforms — no build step, no postinstall network fetch, no manual step for the owner. Lineage: the owner's standing bar, restated at kickoff and sharpened by the ruling that zero-dependency was overvalued. Weight 5 rather than a veto because the owner has already accepted an exposure here.

C4 STRUCTURED OUTPUT — weight 4. Definition: results arrive as typed records — path, line, span, match — rather than text to be scraped. Lineage: R3, R19, R28. Rationale: our boundary is a tool API, not a terminal. Scraping is where line numbers and context get lost, and where a parser silently mis-reads an edge case.

C5 ONE IMPLEMENTATION PER JOB — weight 5. REWRITTEN.
Definition, corrected: adopting a candidate REMOVES the code it replaces, and no second path is kept FOR THE SAME JOB — where a job is defined by THE QUESTION BEING ASKED, not by the surface that answers it.
Lineage: the owner's ruling 'I don't want duplicate code which we never test and never run', and R13's one-writer rule.
WHY IT WAS REWRITTEN, recorded because this criterion produced a wrong decision and a criterion that has misfired must carry its own history: the first pass read C5 as forbidding two search tools and concluded that one tool must answer everything, dropping ripgrep entirely. The owner's counter was not that the weight was too high. It was that the JOB BOUNDARY WAS DRAWN IN THE WRONG PLACE — 'this is not one job, it's two jobs.' Searching a working tree and searching history are different questions with different answers, and answering each with the tool that fits is FIT, not duplication. The defect was in the definition, so the definition is what changed — the weight stays at 5.
THE TEST THIS CRITERION NOW CARRIES, so it cannot misfire the same way twice: before C5 rules a candidate out, name the QUESTION both paths answer. If the two paths answer different questions, C5 does not apply. If they answer the same question, C5 is decisive and the loser is deleted.

C6 BOUNDED COST — weight 3. Definition: every call is bounded in time, result count and per-line width; a pathological input degrades to a capped answer rather than a hang or a context flood. Lineage: R28. Weight 3 because it is achievable at our boundary for almost any candidate, so it discriminates weakly while remaining mandatory in the design.

C7 SELECTION CORRECTNESS — weight 5, and the deciding criterion for D-GUIDANCE. Definition: the mechanism picks the rules that genuinely bind a state, and whether it picked correctly is CHECKABLE rather than a matter of taste. Lineage: R14, R15, R37; need N3. Rationale: a join that pulls in plausible-but-wrong rules is worse than no join, because it costs attention while looking like coverage — and probe P5 proved the obvious mechanism does not exist, so this criterion is doing real work rather than rubber-stamping a foregone choice.

C8 NO MIGRATION DEBT — weight 2. Definition: how much existing ledger data must be rewritten before the mechanism works at all. Lineage: R14, informed by P5's count — ten nodes carry applies_to, zero machine states do. Weight 2 DELIBERATELY LOW: migrating ten nodes is cheap, and letting migration cost dominate would pick the mechanism that fits today's accidental data rather than the one that is right. Recorded so the low weight reads as a decision rather than an oversight.

C9 EVIDENCE FROM OUR OWN FAILURES — weight 5. ADDED.
Definition: where this project has ALREADY observed a candidate or an approach fail, that observation outranks reasoning about how it ought to behave. A design that contradicts a measured local failure must say so explicitly and carry the argument, not pass silently.
Lineage: R8, R19, R31, R34 — every one of which exists because something failed here and was measured — and probes P1, P3, P8, P9, P10, P11.
WHY IT EXISTS: the owner's correction, in their words — 'you don't seem to weight the errors we found today strongly enough.' The first pass ran a criteria set in which nothing represented our own measured history, so a day of observed failures had no channel through which to affect the decision. They lost to a tidy principle. A criteria set that cannot hear evidence will always prefer the elegant answer.
Weight 5, equal to the heaviest: it is not a tiebreaker. Where local evidence and a general principle disagree, the evidence wins unless the difference between our case and the general one is NAMED.
HOW IT SCORES, so it stays a criterion and not a mood: for each candidate, list the observations this project has recorded about it. A candidate with no local history scores neutral — absence of evidence is not evidence.

PRUNED, with reasons, so the vital few are visibly vital: RAW SPEED — every candidate is fast enough at our scale, and the cost that matters is round-trips, already carried by C2 and C4. MATURITY OR POPULARITY — a proxy for what C3 and C6 measure directly. LICENCE — all candidates permissive, no discrimination. EXTENSIBILITY TO OTHER LANGUAGES — real for some candidates, but our product is one TypeScript codebase, so it scores a hypothetical. TOKEN EFFICIENCY — genuinely important, but an OUTCOME of C4 and C6 rather than an independent axis; scoring it separately would double-count.
Nine criteria, under the eleven-criterion ceiling.
